sections.h2: Who handles property tax in Hertford County, NC?
sections.html:
Two offices in the county complex on Justice Drive in Winton split the work. The Tax Assessor lists and values property, and the Tax Collector bills and collects.

Hertford County tax offices as listed on county web pages
OfficeAddressPhoneHours
Tax Assessor115 Justice Drive, Suite 4, Winton252-358-78108:30 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. Monday to Friday
Tax Collector115 Justice Drive, Suite 5, Winton252-358-78158:30 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. Monday to Friday

The assessor's mission is to locate, identify and appraise all taxable real and personal property under Chapter 105 of the General Statutes. The collector bills for the county and also for the towns of Ahoskie, Harrellsville, Cofield, Como, Murfreesboro and Winton, plus two drainage districts, three fire districts and solid waste fees. A Hertford County tax bill can therefore carry several lines depending on where the parcel sits.

sections.h2: When are Hertford County property taxes due?
sections.html:
Taxes are due September 1, and interest starts on January 6 of the following year at 2 percent. After that it grows by three quarters of one percent for each month until the bill is paid.

The county measures lateness by the postal postmark, not the date on a postage meter. Partial payments are accepted from the time the bill arrives until January 6. A bill for a mortgage escrow account still goes to the owner, with the escrow company notified electronically, and the collector relies on the lender to decide which bills it will pay, so contact your lender if you expect it to cover the amount.

  • Pay online, in person at the Winton office, or by phone at 1-888-520-8728.
  • Online card payments carry a 2.5 percent convenience fee, which the county says goes to the payment processor.
  • Card payments are also taken at the counter.
  • A returned check triggers the G.S. 105-357(2) penalty of $25.00 or 10 percent of the check, whichever is greater, up to $1,000.

sections.h2: What does the 2027 Hertford County revaluation change?
sections.html:
New real estate values take effect January 1, 2027. The last revaluation in the county was in 2019, and the state requires reappraisal at least every eight years.

The county's FAQ says appraisers divide the county into market areas, study recent sales, and apply a uniform schedule of values. Field measuring began in July 2025 to fix listing errors and capture changes since the last cycle. Owners get a notice of assessed value shortly after the effective date, and appeal instructions will appear on that notice. The old value can be compared using the parcel's 2018 tax card, which the tax office can pull.

The county states that the purpose is fairness among owners rather than a bigger tax base, and that values will not move uniformly. The commissioners and town boards set the rate, which is typically adopted in June. A bill equals the tax value times the rate, so ask the tax office for the current rate sheet when you plan a sale.

sections.h2: How do I dispute a Hertford County value?
sections.html:
Use the instructions printed on your notice of assessed value. The county says it will also post appeal forms on the Assessor's page as the revaluation date approaches.

The board that hears formal appeals is the Board of Equalization and Review, usually the county commissioners. Its first meeting falls between the first Monday in April and the first Monday in May under G.S. 105-322, and in a revaluation year it finishes by December 1. A written request to be heard has to arrive before the board adjourns. Ask the assessor for the adjournment date, and see G.S. 105-322.

sections.h2: Which tax relief programs apply in Hertford County?
sections.html:
North Carolina lets an owner draw on only one of its three relief programs. All are filed with the county assessor on Form AV-9. The elderly or disabled exclusion, the disabled veteran exclusion and the circuit breaker are described in G.S. 105-277.1, 105-277.1C and 105-277.1B, and the 2026 income limit printed by the Department of Revenue is $38,800.

Ask the Tax Assessor at 252-358-7810 which program fits your situation and whether your application is on file. A sale can end a deferral, so raise it before listing. Form details: NCDOR Form AV-9.

sections.h2: What happens if I sell a Hertford County house with taxes unpaid?
sections.html:
The tax follows the property. A lien for real property taxes attaches on the date the property must be listed, and penalties, interest and costs attach with it under G.S. 105-355. The county's FAQ adds that real property is listed in the name of the owner on January 1 each year, so a seller who conveys after that date can still receive the bill.

Practical steps for a seller:

  • Ask the Tax Collector for the payoff amount for the current and any prior years before the closing date.
  • Have the closing attorney pay taxes from proceeds; the Register of Deeds expects deeds to say delinquent taxes, if any, will be paid that way.
  • Forward any bill that arrives after the sale to the new owner, as the county asks.

If taxes stay unpaid, the collector can use garnishment of wages, bank attachment, attachment of state income tax refunds, levy and foreclosure. The office also offers a three-month payment plan on delinquent taxes. Foreclosure auctions are held at the courthouse door, payment is in full in cash or certified funds, and the sale is advertised in the local newspaper. Properties that do not sell are disposed of by the county.

sections.h2: What vehicles, county-owned land and auctions does the collector handle?
sections.html:
The Tax Collector's pages cover more than house bills. Motor vehicles are billed within 90 days of tag renewal, owners get one month to pay before interest starts, and after four months a block goes on the tag. The county cannot prorate or reduce a vehicle bill without the FS20 receipt from NCDMV, which must reach the office within one year of surrender. The license plate agency in Ahoskie is at 907 E. Memorial Drive.

The office also advertises county-owned property open for bids and foreclosed properties with auction dates. Anyone planning to buy a tax-foreclosed parcel should know that auctions are not registered in advance, since you or a representative simply appear at the courthouse door.

sections.h2: What do the Census figures say about Hertford County owners?
sections.html:
The county counts 8,285 households of about 2.20 people each. Ownership runs at 67.4 percent, the middle home value among owners is $119,200, and median monthly owner costs are $1,285 with a mortgage and $523 without one. Poverty affects 22.9 percent of residents, and 27.1 percent are 65 or older. These figures come from Census QuickFacts.

Modest home values mean that a county bill, a solid waste fee and a fire district charge can weigh on owners with fixed incomes. That is why the exclusions above and the three-month plan for delinquent accounts matter locally.

faqs.q: When are Hertford County property taxes due?
faqs.a: They are due September 1. Interest begins January 6 at 2 percent, then 3/4 of 1 percent per month until paid, measured by the postal postmark.

faqs.q: Who sends the tax bill in Hertford County?
faqs.a: The Hertford County Tax Collector bills for the county, six towns, fire districts, drainage districts and solid waste fees. The office is at 115 Justice Drive, Suite 5, Winton, and its phone is 252-358-7815.

faqs.q: When does the next Hertford County revaluation take effect?
faqs.a: January 1, 2027. The last one was in 2019, and owners receive notices of their new assessed values shortly after that date, with appeal instructions on the notice.

faqs.q: I sold my house but still got the Hertford County bill. Why?
faqs.a: North Carolina lists real property in the owner's name as of January 1, so the bill can be issued to the prior owner. Send a copy to the new owner and tell the Tax Collector, as the county asks.

faqs.q: Can I pay Hertford County taxes over time?
faqs.a: Partial payments are accepted until January 6, and the collector offers a three-month payment plan on delinquent taxes. Call 252-358-7815 to arrange it.
